pr_title: Don't track LHASH op counts when tracing disabled
pr_comments: I am not sure coupling this with trace enabled is the right thing. Perhaps another build time option should be added?
I'm open to it. Any suggestions for what it should be called? LHASH_DEBUG?
LHASH_STATS? Or just STATISTICS? I.e., no-statistics and OPENSSL_NO_STATISTICS so some further statistics could be enabled/disabled by it if we had any.
Updated to use a new option stats/OPENSSL_NO_STATS.
I'd be fine removing the statistics entirely.

> I'd be fine removing the statistics entirely.

IMO that could be done only in 4.0 or with an OMC exception.

> Approving for master. For 3.0 branch it would IMO need an OTC exception.

Doesn't it need an exception even for master since it won't be ABI compatible?

The internal structure of lhash_st isn't exposed as part of the ABI, is it?

The output of `OPENSSL_LH_stats_bio` changes, but I'm not sure that should be considered part of the "ABI". The manpage for `OPENSSL_LH_stats` doesn't define the output as having any specific format, or the output as being intended for machine consumption. Many of the existing values are also not emitted already if locking fails.

> Doesn't it need an exception even for master since it won't be ABI compatible?

Well, the function printing the stats is kept, it just won't produce any useful output. But yeah.

> The output of OPENSSL_LH_stats_bio changes, but I'm not sure that should be considered part of the "ABI".

That's the bit I'm worried about. It is entirely feasible that applications are relying on that output. That said I don't expect this to break very many applications if any - so I'm not against the change. But I do think it needs to be agreed. Incidentally we have a "Policy on API compatibility in minor releases" which says "No changes to existing public API functions and data are permitted":

https://beta.openssl.org/policies/technical/api-compat.html

Now that we try and apply that policy to this case it strikes me as a little vague and broad. Presumably we are allowed to fix bugs and refactor code - so "no changes" seems not quite right.
**OTC to decide:** The stats using atomics are really expensive, can we disable them by default and if so, on which branches?

> No changes to existing public API functions and data are permitted

That was meant to be public API function signatures and data.

> That was meant to be public API function signatures and data.

I think at least the functional behaviour is expected to remain the same as well (excluding bugs).
INSTALL.md and CHANGES.md updated. I also updated the manpage.

issue_context.title: LHASH statistical counter performance overheads (cache contention)
issue_context.body:
Currently LHASH has a number of statistical counters like `num_hash_calls`, `num_comp_calls`, `num_retrieve`, `num_retrieve_miss` and `num_hash_comps`. These are incremented using atomics during retrieval operations, which creates possible cache contention issues with high amounts of parallelism. This causes `getrn` to sometimes be more costly than it needs to be.

This seems needless since these statistics are probably very rarely used in production. They are only used by various OPENSSL_LH_ statistical functions which output text reports to BIOs.

Possibly we should simply compile these out when `OPENSSL_NO_TRACE` is defined (or another define if someone has a better suggestion).

It is a valid question whether the other LHASH counters should also be compiled out in this case. Since these other counters are only touched on mutating LHASH operations, they do not use atomics because the caller of LHASH mutation operations has responsibility for synchronization. But for consistency and performance we may as well compile these out at the same time.

It is possible this is a cause of #16791 (MSQUIC handshakes per second performance regression) but this is mostly speculative on my part, and based on extrapolating profiling run on my machine to how that profiling might perform when extrapolated to a very high-core-count server.

review_comments:
Personally, I'd remove this #ifdef and the prior #endif and have the function output _nothing_ in a no-stats build.

The same could apply to the other functions here because they are all about statistics presentation.
